Axes.description: The three seasonal axes, each in -1..1. Filled by the features stage.
Axes.title: Axes

Classifier.description:
Which classifier decided the season, and how far to trust it.

Present only when a season was actually computed - a refused photo has no
seasons and nothing to say about them.

version.description: Version of the classifier DATA (src/color_engine/data/classifier.json), not of the package. Every anchor point, weight and prototype lives there, so this is the thing that changes when seasons start coming out differently.
version.title: Version

draft.description: True while the anchor points and prototypes are reasoned rather than measured. Nothing in this classifier has been checked against faces a stylist labelled, because there is no such set yet. Consumers must say so to the user.
draft.title: Draft

low_confidence.description: Confidence fell below the data file's min_confidence_for_season. The season is still the best available reading - this says how much of one it is.
low_confidence.title: Low Confidence

exclusions.description: Every feature the classifier could not use, with its reason. Empty when it had everything.
exclusions.title: Exclusions

confidence.description: How the confidence was arrived at. Null when no season was placed.

Classifier.title: Classifier

ConfidenceBreakdown.description:
The confidence, taken apart into what made it.

``final`` is the product of the three. Published whole because a number
somebody is expected to act on should be arguable, and it cannot be argued
with unless the argument is visible.

margin.description: The RAW gap between the top two scores. Zero on a dead heat. Reported beside `from_margin` rather than folded into it, because the two are different numbers and a page showing one under the other's name is worse than showing neither: the first live frame had two seasons tied at 0.1445 and the label 'how far the first season is ahead of the second' read 0.150.
margin.title: Margin

from_margin.description: That gap put through the confidence curve. Never zero - a dead heat still earns the curve's floor, because the season is still the best available reading.
from_margin.title: From Margin

features_factor.description: What the missing or excluded zones cost.
features_factor.title: Features Factor

quality_factor.description: What the photograph cost: white balance, exposure, uneven light - everything the earlier stages concluded, multiplied together.
quality_factor.title: Quality Factor

ConfidenceBreakdown.title: ConfidenceBreakdown

Contrast.description: Contrast measures between zones. Filled by the features stage.

value.description: Overall value contrast: spread of L* across hair, skin and eyes.
value.title: Value

hair_skin.description: L* distance between hair and skin.
hair_skin.title: Hair Skin

eye_skin.description: L* distance between iris and skin.
eye_skin.title: Eye Skin

iris_sclera.description: L* distance between the iris and the white of the same eye. The second contrast the classifier reads, and the one that separates a dark-eyed light blonde from a light-eyed one.
iris_sclera.title: Iris Sclera

Contrast.title: Contrast

ExcludedFeature.description:
One input the classifier did not have, and why.

In the contract rather than only in the debug artifacts, for the same reason
``ZoneStatus`` is: a confidence of 0.31 with no explanation is an assertion,
and the page that has to justify it to a stylist is a consumer of this
contract, not a reader of our debug objects.

feature.description: The feature name in the classifier data file.
feature.title: Feature

reason.description: dyed_hair, hair_not_measured, iris_not_measured, sclera_not_measured, skin_not_measured, skin_too_neutral, contrast_not_measured.
reason.title: Reason

ExcludedFeature.title: ExcludedFeature

EyeParts.description:
One eye zone measured on each side separately.

Left and right are the SUBJECT's, as everywhere in this package - the
subject's left eye is on the right of a frontal photo.

These exist because ``zones`` promises a verdict for ``iris_left`` and
``iris_right`` and there was nowhere to put the measurement behind it. A
consumer rendering a row per zone got "not measured" for a side that had in
fact been measured perfectly well, with no reason beside it, because the
side was usable and so had nothing to explain.
EyeParts.title: EyeParts

LabSample.description: One zone, measured in CIELAB (D65, CIE 1931 2 degree observer).

C.description: Chroma, hypot(a*, b*), computed from the median a*/b*.
C.title: C

h.description: Hue angle in degrees, 0..360, from the median a*/b*.
h.title: H

pixels.description: Pixels that survived masking and outlier rejection.
pixels.title: Pixels

L_iqr.description: Interquartile range of L* in the zone - how uniform the sample is.
L_iqr.title: L Iqr

LabSample.title: LabSample

RejectReason.description: Why a photo cannot be analysed. Stable strings - Laravel maps them to copy.
RejectReason.title: RejectReason

Samples.description:
Measured colour per zone.

``None`` means nothing was measured: the zone was absent, or too little of
it survived masking to measure at all.

**Not** "the zone was rejected." A zone that produced a sample keeps its
numbers here however it was then judged, and ``zones`` carries the verdict
beside them. They used to be cleared together, which threw away the one
thing a rejection is worth reviewing on: "darker_than_skin" does not say how
much darker, so nobody could tell a rule that missed by 1 L* from one that
missed by 30, and a threshold nobody can see the margin on cannot be argued
with.

Nothing downstream measures with a rejected zone - the aggregates and the
classifier read the verdict, not the presence of numbers.

skin.description: Pooled sample over the skin sub-zones that were usable. Not always all three: a blown cheek is measured, reported, and left out of this.

iris.description: Both irises pooled - over the pixels each eye kept, and only from the eyes that passed every check. Never a fresh measurement of the union of the masks, which would re-admit what each eye's own filtering threw out.

iris_parts.description: Each iris on its own, whatever the verdict on it. A side that was rejected keeps its numbers here and is not in `iris` above.

sclera.description: Both scleras pooled, on the same rule.

sclera_parts.description: Each sclera on its own, whatever the verdict on it. A side that was rejected keeps its numbers here and is not in `sclera` above.

Samples.title: Samples

Season.description: The 12 seasons. Slugs are the contract; never localise these.
Season.title: Season

SkinParts.description: The three skin sub-zones, each measured on its own.
SkinParts.title: SkinParts

WhiteBalance.description: What was done about the light, and how sure we are of it.

enabled.description: Whether the white-balance step was switched on for this run at all. Separate from `method` because 'we did not try' and 'we tried and could not' are different answers, and only one of them is about the photograph.
enabled.title: Enabled

reason.description: Why `method` is `none`. Null when a correction was applied.

method.description: Which reference the illuminant was estimated from.

single_eye.description: True when only one sclera was usable, so the estimate rests on one eye.
single_eye.title: Single Eye

correction_strength.description: How far the estimated illuminant sat from D65, as Euclidean distance in CIE 1976 u'v'. 0 when nothing was applied. Beyond a threshold the photo is rejected as color_cast instead of corrected.
correction_strength.title: Correction Strength

estimated_cct.description: Correlated colour temperature of the estimated illuminant in kelvin, or null when there is no estimate or it sits too far off the Planckian locus to mean anything.
estimated_cct.title: Estimated Cct

target_calibrated.description: Whether the sclera's target chromaticity has been measured on a real reference set. False means the correction is pulling the sclera to exact neutral, which a healthy sclera is not, and every result carries a systematic cool bias of that size. Consumers should treat an uncalibrated result as provisional.
target_calibrated.title: Target Calibrated

WhiteBalance.title: WhiteBalance

WhiteBalanceMethod.description:
Where the illuminant estimate came from.

The order is the order of preference: the sclera is the only near-neutral
reference a face reliably carries, the scene behind the person is the
fallback, and ``none`` means neither could be trusted and the samples are
reported as measured. Skin is never a reference - correcting the light
against it would absorb the undertone the analysis exists to measure.
WhiteBalanceMethod.title: WhiteBalanceMethod

WhiteBalanceReason.description:
Why ``method`` came out ``none``.

``method: none`` on its own cannot be read. It covers a deployment that
never wanted correction, a frame whose eyes were unusable, and a frame whose
background was too dark to estimate from - three different things, only one
of which is a fact about the photograph. A page showing the first as though
it were the second sends somebody off to retake a photo that was fine.
WhiteBalanceReason.title: WhiteBalanceReason

ZoneStatus.description:
Whether a zone may be measured WITH, and why not when it may not.

Not the same question as whether ``samples`` has numbers for it. A blown
cheek and a sclera that read as lid shadow are both measured and both
reported; this is what says they were not used.

"sclera: null" in ``samples`` is not an answer anybody can act on - a closed
eye, a mask that missed, an eye too small in the original frame and an eye
whose two halves disagreed all look identical from there. The reason existed
all along; it just lived in the debug artifacts, where a consumer of the
contract could not see it.

usable.description: May this zone be measured WITH? False covers both 'nothing was measured' and 'measured, and then ruled out' - `samples` says which, by whether it has numbers for it.
usable.title: Usable

reason.description: Why not: too_few_pixels, eye_too_small, too_dark, too_noisy, overexposed, not_brighter_than_iris, darker_than_skin, more_chromatic_than_skin, eyes_disagree. Null when the zone is usable.
reason.title: Reason

ZoneStatus.title: ZoneStatus

description:
What ``Engine.analyze`` returns and what the HTTP layer will serve.

Non-contract extras (debug artifacts, step timings) live in private
attributes exposed as properties, so they never leak into ``to_json``.

reject_reason.description: Set if and only if status == 'rejected'.

source_color_space.description: ICC profile found in the input, or 'sRGB (assumed)' when untagged.
source_color_space.title: Source Color Space

samples.description: Measured colour per zone, already adapted to D65 when white balance was applied. The uncorrected values live in the debug artifacts, never in the contract.

zones.description: Per-zone verdict, keyed by the engine's own zone names: skin, left_cheek, right_cheek, forehead, hair, iris, iris_left, iris_right, sclera, sclera_left, sclera_right. Empty when the photo was refused before any zone was built.
zones.title: Zones

seasons.description: Top 2 seasons, best first. Empty until classification.
seasons.title: Seasons

confidence.description: How much to trust the season call.
confidence.title: Confidence

classifier.description: Which classifier produced the seasons. Null when none ran.

algo_version.description: Package version that produced this result.
algo_version.title: Algo Version

title: ColorEngineAnalysisResult
